punchline: In Warren Berger's telling, Netflix grew out of one annoyed question about a late fee.
thirty_sec: Reed Hastings got hit with a late fee on a video rental. Instead of just paying it, he asked why renting had to work that way. That led to a what-if: a subscription. Warren Berger uses the story to show a pattern: ask why first, then what if, and only then work out how. Most of us skip straight to how.
question: What's an everyday annoyance you've just accepted without ever asking why it exists?
